additional_concerns: The legacy exclusions in node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 implement a proposed inference: preservation of application processing defeats relief for the change. The source expressly preserves processing, but does not expressly establish an enduring substantive disqualification, including after withdrawal, resubmission or subsequent disposition. Those alternatives remain unresolved.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question rather than determining their eligibility. Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa answers only substantive qualification. Neither result resolves actual relief for a pending legacy application.

The introduction describes immediate effect, while the implementation provision specifies 28 November 2025 for measures in the FAQs. The supplied date tests follow the specific implementation provision, but the relevant assessment event and its relationship to proposed implementation remain unconfirmed.

Additional authority needed to resolve actual procedural relief includes the relevant updated FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds and authoritative clarification of legacy-application treatment and commencement. Applicable home-jurisdiction rules are also needed to determine home compliance in an actual case. These materials are absent; the packet does not identify which unnamed dependency ID corresponds to which authority, so no catalogue mapping is inferred.
Node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 supplies no executable formalization. Its unresolved actual-relief question must not be treated as either executable success or substantive failure.

All executable classifications remain supplied judgments. The formulas do not independently determine materiality, home compliance, novelty, complexity or possible local policy implications. Removal of prior approval does not establish satisfaction of notification, filing or continuing post-vetting obligations.
